entities.summary: François Vatable (1466-1547) was a French humanist scholar, hellenist, and hebraist. Born in Burgundy, France, he studied at the University of Paris and later at the University of Ferrara. Vatable's significant contributions include his translations of classical Greek and Hebrew texts, which helped to revive interest in ancient learning and promote cross-cultural understanding. He also collaborated with prominent intellectuals, such as Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples, and contributed to the development of biblical scholarship. Vatable's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing later scholars and shaping the course of Western intellectual history. He is remembered for his meticulous scholarship and dedication to preserving ancient texts, which continues to inspire scholars today. François Vatable's work had a lasting impact on the study of classical languages and biblical interpretation, earning him a place among the most influential humanists of the Renaissance.

He was a prominent figure in the translation of classical texts, particularly those of Aristotle and Xenophon, and his work had a significant impact on the field of biblical studies. Vatable's most notable achievement was the publication of the first complete translation of the Hebrew Bible into French, a groundbreaking work that helped to spread Jewish studies and biblical scholarship throughout Europe. Vatable's legacy can be seen in the many scholars who followed in his footsteps, including the great humanist and theologian, Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples. This remarkable scholar's contributions to the fields of classical studies, biblical scholarship, and humanism continue to be felt to this day. Vatable's life and work serve as a testament to the power of human curiosity and the enduring importance of classical learning in shaping our understanding of the world.
